acceptance_criteria: Structured multi-agent final review remains available as an advisory MCP service without claiming Codex runtime authority.
Lifecycle and final-review coordination tools are exposed from the installed plugin root.
Editor, runner, repository-local, repository-remote, and diagnostics mutation capabilities remain unavailable from the plugin-wide surface.
All release artifacts, manifests, tests, and documentation describe and ship the same advisory surface.
explicit_concerns: Do not restore unsupported Codex boundary enforcement.
Do not expose project mutation tools.
Review the public MCP behavior, source-to-binary parity, versioning, and installed-root startup.
context.user_request: Restore the structured multi-agent review process that was unintentionally removed from the reduced bootstrap plugin while keeping the plugin advisory and withholding project mutation tools.

shared_test_evidence.summary: Strict Rust formatting and Clippy passed; 344 coordinator tests and 20 capability tests passed serially; source-to-release parity passed; all eight MCP startup tests passed, including the top-level Claude manifest; repository pre-commit gate passed after the cross-harness fix.

lens_objectives.agent-instruction-quality: Review whether plugin, skill, and MCP instructions accurately preserve the structured multi-agent workflow without claiming unsupported authority.
lens_objectives.architecture-maintainability: Identify evidence-backed failure modes caused by incoherent ownership boundaries, unsafe coupling, or complexity that makes the changed behavior difficult to modify or verify; do not report style preferences alone.
lens_objectives.correctness-behavior: Verify functional correctness, edge cases, state transitions, and behavioral regressions.
lens_objectives.operability-user-impact: Check runtime failure handling, diagnostics, operator impact, usability for changed user-facing behavior, and accessibility for changed interactive surfaces.
lens_objectives.production-risk-footguns: Identify production-scale failure modes such as resource exhaustion, unbounded retries or cardinality, unsafe defaults, burst behavior, and excessive data access.
lens_objectives.release-integration: Check only versioning, compatibility, packaging, documentation, CI, rollout, and downstream-integration obligations implied by the changed release surface.
lens_objectives.safety-human-harm: Identify plausible failures that could harm people or the physical world in the system's intended deployment.
lens_objectives.security-safety: Identify unauthorized-access, protected-data, trust-boundary, integrity, and abuse-resistance regressions introduced by the change.
lens_objectives.tests-verification: Assess whether tests and verification evidence cover the changed behavior and plausible failure modes.

subagent_lifecycle.policy: Start a fresh lens subagent for every review iteration and lens. Carry continuity only through this MCP state, prior defenses, and caller decisions. Close each assigned subagent after its result is collected.

dimensions.evidence: The pinned diff replaces the plugin-read-only surface with plugin-advisory and admits all existing workflow.* and final_review.* tools while retaining reader and setup tools. This is a material expansion of public behavior across both harness manifests and four bundled binaries. The supplied exact-diff shared evidence reports coordinator, capability, source-parity, release-completeness, startup, and pre-commit success.
dimensions.material_impact: Structured review or lifecycle coordination could be unavailable or behave incorrectly for installed users, or the plugin could cross the intended advisory boundary.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A surface-selection or dispatch defect could make the installed plugin omit required lifecycle/review tools, route a newly exposed tool incorrectly, or admit a non-advisory service, causing the restored review workflow to fail or violate its capability contract.

dimensions.evidence: The sole supplied broad evidence is bound to diff hash 7155c1062ea6c312b6745d1882cd524d1b60bf92 and reports 344 coordinator tests, 20 capability tests, source-to-release parity, all eight startup tests, strict Rust checks, and the repository pre-commit gate passing. The diff adds direct allowlist and installed-manifest coverage, but four platform artifacts are shipped and this scout did not execute them independently as required.
dimensions.material_impact: The advisory coordinator could fail to start or expose the intended tools on one supported target even though repository-wide source and packaging checks pass.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A platform-specific runtime or launcher defect could remain despite structural release checks and host-executable startup coverage, especially on non-host architectures.

dimensions.evidence: ServiceSurface::PluginAdvisory permits only the explicit reader/setup set plus workflow.* and final_review.* prefixes, and handle_json_rpc rejects disallowed names before semantic dispatch. Changed capability tests directly deny workspace-editor.patch and assert that every advertised name belongs to the advisory allowlist. The intended deployment is a trusted, single-owner local development plugin, not an isolation boundary against malicious local processes.
dimensions.material_impact: A local project asset or repository state could be modified through a plugin surface documented as withholding editor, runner, repository, and diagnostics services.
dimensions.plausible_failure: An overlooked dispatch alias or future tool added under an admitted prefix could cross from advisory state coordination into project mutation without a corresponding boundary review.

dimensions.evidence: The change is a local coding-plugin coordination and packaging update with no safety-critical device, physical process, medical workflow, or other human-harm exposure path in the intended deployment.

The change reuses the existing WorkflowCore tool families through one new ServiceSurface variant rather than duplicating coordinator implementations. Source, manifests, documentation, tests, release metadata, and binaries are changed together. Prefix admission makes the public boundary dependent on future naming discipline.
dimensions.material_impact: A later extension could silently broaden the installed plugin surface and increase coupling between naming and capability policy.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A future workflow.* or final_review.* tool with effects beyond advisory coordination would become public automatically because the surface is prefix-based rather than an immutable explicit inventory.

dimensions.evidence: The installed service selector changes name from plugin-read-only to plugin-advisory in the component, Claude, and Codex manifests; the default binary surface changes accordingly; and four release binaries are replaced. Startup checks reportedly pass for all eight cases, including installed-root and top-level Claude coverage, but successful native execution on every shipped architecture is not directly available to this scout.
dimensions.material_impact: Users on an affected harness or architecture would lose the structured review service at startup or receive misleading capability discovery.
dimensions.plausible_failure: A stale launcher, manifest argument, binary, or platform-specific artifact could reject plugin-advisory or expose the wrong inventory when invoked from an installed plugin root.

dimensions.evidence: The marketplace and top-level plugin versions move from 5.0.1 to 5.0.2, component manifests move from 0.19.1 to 0.19.2, all binary checksums and the source fingerprint change, and both harness manifests select plugin-advisory. Supplied release-completeness and source-parity gates passed for the pinned diff.
dimensions.material_impact: One marketplace or architecture could distribute stale behavior or fail installation/startup while other release surfaces appear correct.
dimensions.plausible_failure: Any unnoticed mismatch among marketplace metadata, per-harness manifests, bundled binaries, release fingerprints, or launcher arguments could ship a version whose installed behavior differs by harness or target.

dimensions.evidence: The service is a bounded local stdio MCP for a single-owner development environment; request limits, existing coordinator bounds, and capability filtering remain in place. The change makes stateful workflow and review coordination available by default, increasing ordinary exposure to stale or interrupted local coordination state without adding a network service.
dimensions.material_impact: A development session could be delayed, incorrectly gated, or require local recovery, but project mutation remains outside this surface and the state is documented as local and rebuildable where applicable.
dimensions.plausible_failure: Interrupted or concurrent local sessions could leave durable advisory workflow/review state that a later agent mistakes for current coordination state if recovery and supersession paths have an undiscovered edge case.

dimensions.evidence: Changed MCP instructions and both READMEs repeatedly state that coordination is advisory, does not execute project mutations, and does not restrict ordinary Codex tools; they also distinguish future standalone Tiber enforcement. The same public vocabulary includes lifecycle authorization and delivery-gate tool names, so correct agent interpretation depends on preserving that qualification across skill, tool-description, and manifest contexts.
dimensions.material_impact: The agent could make an unauthorized external-action inference, misreport enforcement guarantees, or block/advance work based on a capability the Codex runtime does not enforce.
dimensions.plausible_failure: An agent could interpret workflow authorization transitions as runtime permission or enforcement rather than advisory process state, or infer that ordinary mutation tools are restricted by the MCP.

plan_assumptions: The review scope is the complete uncommitted change pinned to baseline commit a742cc8e8e5b20ec15a328077a04d31f13ad224e and the supplied 22-path inventory; the movable base was not re-resolved.
The supplied shared test evidence is accepted as the sole broad test run for this assessment; no tests or verifier were invoked by the scout.

The intended threat model is the repository's local single-owner development-tool model, which trusts the owner, installed toolchain, environment, and local configuration and does not treat intentional local self-bypass as an in-model attacker.
Non-host platform runtime behavior is inferred from the supplied source-to-release and release-completeness evidence, so remaining cross-platform uncertainty selects deeper coverage.

The manifest, source, documentation, tests, release metadata, and binary changes form one cohesive advisory-surface release increment and do not provide independently shippable delivery boundaries for a split.
